caption:
Most bone grafts used in India are still imported. A Maharashtra company just got government backing to 3D-print them here instead.

India's Technology Development Board sanctioned support for Ceramat Private Limited, based in Palghar, Maharashtra, to commercialise 3D-printed patient-specific bone grafts - combining Digital Light Processing and extrusion-based 3D printing. The grafts are built from indigenously manufactured bioceramic materials - hydroxyapatite, tricalcium phosphate and bioactive glass - not imported raw material, and unlike standard grafts, they're shaped to match each patient's own anatomy.

A part of the body that used to arrive from abroad - now printed to fit, at home.
